facts.fact: Streaming services capture approximately 46% of all primetime television viewing in the United States, according to Nielsen's Gauge data from June 2025, as cited by Adwave.
facts.quote: Streaming services now capture approximately 46% of all primetime television viewing in the United States

facts.fact: Nielsen reported that streaming reached a record 46% share of total TV viewing in June 2025.
facts.quote: streaming services reached a record 46% share of total TV viewing in June 2025

facts.fact: Nielsen data cited by Adwave shows broadcast held a 20.1% share and cable a 24.1% share of TV viewing, with streaming exceeding their combined share for the first time.
facts.quote: the combined share of broadcast (20.1%) and cable (24.1%) television

facts.fact: Streaming usage increased by 71% from May 2021 to May 2025, according to Adwave's citation of Nielsen data.
facts.quote: streaming usage increased by 71%

facts.fact: From May 2021 to May 2025, broadcast viewing declined by 21%, according to Adwave's summary of the data.
facts.quote: broadcast viewing declined by 21%

facts.fact: From May 2021 to May 2025, cable viewing dropped by 39%, according to Adwave's summary of the data.
facts.quote: cable viewing dropped by 39%

facts.fact: According to CNBC as cited by Adwave, YouTube leads all streaming platforms during primetime hours with 12.5% of total TV viewing.
facts.quote: YouTube leads all streaming platforms during primetime hours, capturing 12.5% of total TV viewing as reported by

facts.fact: According to TV Technology as cited by Adwave, Netflix's primetime usage rose 13.5% month over month in June 2025 to an 8.3% share.
facts.quote: increasing its usage by 13.5% to reach 8.3% share

facts.fact: Adwave lists Amazon Prime Video at 3.2% of total TV viewing, without naming a source for the figure.
facts.quote: Amazon Prime Video: 3.2% of total TV viewing

facts.fact: Adwave lists Hulu at 2.6% of total TV viewing, without naming a source for the figure.
facts.quote: Hulu: 2.6% of total TV viewing

facts.fact: Adwave lists Disney+ at 1.9% of total TV viewing, without naming a source for the figure.
facts.quote: Disney+: 1.9% of total TV viewing

facts.fact: Adwave states that viewers aged 18-34 stream during roughly 65% of their primetime viewing hours.
facts.quote: Viewers aged 18-34 stream during roughly 65% of their primetime viewing hours.

facts.fact: Adwave states that viewers aged 35-49 show streaming at approximately 50% of primetime viewing.
facts.quote: Viewers aged 35-49 show more balanced patterns at approximately 50%.

facts.fact: Adwave states that viewers aged 50-64 show streaming at about 35% of primetime viewing.
facts.quote: Viewers aged 50-64 maintain stronger traditional TV habits at about 35% streaming.

facts.fact: Adwave states that viewers 65 and older show streaming at approximately 25% of evening viewing.
facts.quote: Viewers 65 and older show streaming at approximately 25% of evening viewing.

facts.fact: According to Nielsen as cited by Adwave, streaming accounts for 44.8% of all U.S. TV viewing.
facts.quote: streaming now accounts for 44.8% of all U.S. TV viewing

facts.fact: According to TV Technology as cited by Adwave, over 73% of TV viewing is ad-supported.
facts.quote: Over 73% of TV viewing is ad-supported

facts.fact: Adwave states that through its platform businesses can start TV advertising with budgets as low as $30 a day.
facts.quote: allows businesses to start with budgets as low as $30 a day

facts.fact: Adwave recommends that most local businesses allocate $300-500 to primetime hours over a two-week campaign to build recognition.
facts.quote: allocating $300-500 specifically to primetime hours over a two-week campaign

facts.fact: Adwave states that traditional broadcast network primetime commands CPMs of $30-50 or more.
facts.quote: Traditional broadcast network primetime commands CPMs of $30-50+.

facts.fact: Adwave states that streaming primetime CPMs average $20-30, with many FAST channels and programmatic options running $15-25.
facts.quote: Streaming primetime CPMs average $20-30, with many FAST channels and programmatic options running $15-25.

facts.fact: Adwave identifies 7-10 PM as the peak streaming hours for primetime.
facts.quote: Schedule campaigns for 7-10 PM when streaming peaks

facts.fact: Adwave states that traditional broadcast primetime runs 8-11 PM Eastern.
facts.quote: Traditional broadcast primetime runs 8-11 PM Eastern.
